summary: 18 claims on what WakeCap says in public, each read from a full-text page dump or two separate reads on 2026-10-05. Labels used: Project A is the Saudi oil and gas mega-site (first case study on the Results page), Project B is the Saudi giga-project with 78 mega-projects (second), Project C is the 78-story tower in Dubai (third), Project D is a second Saudi oil and gas site in the Nov 2025 article. Most useful for the story: the public Platform page already lists Connected Environment (weather, dust, noise dashboards) as a Connected Site module next to Equipment Tracker; the home page shows six sources feeding one knowledge graph; and a WakeCap article gives the reading path (hard-hat sensor, Wirepas mesh, solar gateways on CCTV poles, over 18 months of battery). All outcome numbers are vendor-reported: Project A 94% fewer violations (230 to 15 a month) and 10x faster permits; observation closure from 86 hours to 3 hours; Project B SAR 77 saved per worker per day and SAR 8B+ projected; Project C $3.57M labor value unlocked; 14x ROI on one program; more than 150 million labor hours and $120B+ in active projects. Watch-outs: WakeCap pages disagree in places ($3.5M vs $3.57M, over-reporting vs overtime, 90% vs 91%), digital work permits are tagged 'Soon' on the home page but listed as a module on the Platform page, and no public page mentions lightning, gas or a weather station or says how Heat Stress is computed.

The safety page prints the same numbers as '94% Fewer safety violations', '230→15 Observations per month', '6,875 Hours saved' and '100% Platform uptime' under 'Measured on a [Project A] mega-site' (https://www.wakecap.com/real-time-safety-management), so the wording differs (violations vs observations). (https://www.wakecap.com/about-wakecap), with offices in Dammam (HQ), San Francisco, Dubai and São Paulo. Earlier releases show project value rising while hours stay fixed: 'US$80 billion' with 'more than 150 million labor hours' in May 2025 (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/wakecap-raises-us-28-million-130000979.html), 'over $100B' with '150+ million worker hours' in Oct 2025 (https://www.wakecap.com/news/wakecap-partners-with-nemetschek), 'US$120 billion' in Nov 2025 (https://www.wakecap.com/news/wakecap-acquires-trackfy). Because the hours figure is the same from May 2025 to June 2026, read it as 'at least 150 million', not a live count. Fetched 2026-10-05.

claims.figure: No number. One sentence in the section 'Where the Industry is Headed'.
claims.measures: Status: plan (public positioning in an article; no product page backs it). Find: last third of the article, section 'Where the Industry is Headed'. It follows 'Real-time visibility across thousands of workers.' and 'AI-driven safety observations that turn raw data into actionable insights.' The article does not say the integration is shipped. The only public weather product line is the Connected Environment module on the Platform page (https://www.wakecap.com/platform). Fetched 2026-10-05 as a full-text dump.
claims.source_title: What It Takes to Deploy Smart Safety Tech at Scale

gaps: No public WakeCap page mentions lightning, gas detection or a weather station product. Connected Environment appears only as a one-line module on the Platform page (weather, dust, noise), and it is not one of the six data sources drawn on the home page.

No public number for workers tracked today, number of customers, or number of projects. The 'more than 150 million labor hours' figure is unchanged in releases from May 2025 to June 2026, so it is a floor, not a live count.
Every outcome number is vendor-reported. No baseline, period, method or independent audit is printed. A trade publication (2026-08-16) says the same about the case numbers.

WakeCap pages disagree: $3.5M (Connected Workers page) vs $3.57M (Results page); '96% less over-reporting' (Results page) vs '96% less overtime' (Sep 2025 article); 90% (Sep 2025) vs 91% (May 2025) fewer safety issues; '230 violations' vs '230 observations' a month; the Productivity page gives $3.57M and 60pp to a Saudi oil and gas site while the Results page gives them to a Dubai tower and a Saudi giga-project.

Work permits: the Platform page lists a Digital Work Permit module and the safety page lists 'NextGen Work Permit', but the home page tags the source that holds digital work permits as 'Soon'. The only permit numbers are '10x Faster permits' (Project A) and the acquired company's 25% shorter issuance time.
Heat Stress: no public method, threshold, index (such as WBGT) or sensor type. Only a module name, 'alerts tied to location', and a 2024 partnership with a Japanese heat-warning watch maker.

The WebSearch budget (200 of 200 for the session) ran out before the last two searches (Digital Clinic wording on wakecap.com, Gulf press on WakeCap heat monitoring). I did not route around it. A WakeCap social post about the 2024 heat-watch MOU and a Gulf trade article (HTTP 403) were not fetched.

Figures about '22 million active hours across 15 major projects' and '91% reduction in safety incidents' (older wording) appeared only in a search summary of third-party pages and were not fetched, so they are not used.
No Series A release was found on wakecap.com. The May 2025 figures come from a wire copy (ACCESS Newswire via Yahoo Finance) and a regional news site, both fetched.

Customer, project and people names are printed on the source pages (and in some page anchors). They are redacted here as Project A to D, and anchors are dropped from URLs. To re-check: on the Results page the case cards run Project A, B, C in that order.

Rule conflict flagged: the hard rules say make no network call to any WakeCap host, but this slice requires reading public wakecap.com pages with WebFetch. Only the public marketing site and public news pages were read. No app, API, test or production host was contacted.

WebFetch reads pages through a small model. Each figure was checked in a verbatim full-text dump of the page or in two separate reads, not in raw HTML. An engineer should use Ctrl+F on the page for the quoted phrase.
